attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. He says he saw further converging evidence; the tweets he quotes are other people's and are not his claims.

semantics.note: Faithful. Marcus states as fact that more evidence of tokenmaxxing's decline appeared in late May 2026. No hedging, and there are no conditions to keep.

contract.note: Marcus gave no measure. The plain reading (several developments pointing to a retreat from usage-for-its-own-sake incentives) is ordinary and fair. Leaving out raw price moves is reasonable. Requiring multiple developments inside May 21-29 decides the result.

evidence.note: Business Insider, May 29: an Amazon spokesperson confirmed KiroRank was deprecated, and an SVP told staff not to use AI just to use AI. This is one concrete retreat, inside the window.

Fortune column, May 28, summarising reports. The Meta leaderboard removal is undated and the Microsoft change predates the window. It is secondary commentary that agrees with the thesis, so it does not independently establish a second development in the window.
The Verge, May 14, before the window. Microsoft replaced Claude Code with Copilot CLI and Anthropic models stay available, which weakens the Microsoft case as a cut in usage incentives.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows one well-documented retreat in the window: Amazon deprecated KiroRank and gave explicit guidance against using AI for its own sake. The other examples are undated (Meta), fall before the window and involve a tool switch (Microsoft), or are cost and price signals the contract excludes. The support condition needs multiple independent developments and is not met. Nothing contradicts the claim either. So the evidence does not settle it.
